figurative_meaning_en: An ignorant leader among a group of fools
similar_in_english: In the land of the blind, the one-eyed man is king
example_sentences_in_bangla: এই দলে সবাই অযোগ্য, তাই সে অন্ধের দেশে কানা রাজা হয়ে উঠেছে।
প্রতিযোগিতায় সকলে দুর্বল, এখানে সামান্য যোগ্য ব্যক্তিই অন্ধের দেশে কানা রাজা।
example_sentences_in_english: In this team, everyone is incompetent, so he has become the one-eyed king in the land of the blind.
In a competition where all are weak, even a slightly capable person becomes the one-eyed king in the land of the blind.
history: This proverb is a Bengali adaptation of a Latin saying attributed to Desiderius Erasmus: 'In regione caecorum rex est luscus,' meaning the same idea of relative superiority in a group of inferiors.
note: The idiom highlights relative competence in contexts of widespread inadequacy.
